argDocs.relaxTime: time (in seconds) for the amplitude adjustment to be released (control signal below thresh ). Usually longer than clampTime ; depending on the input and control signal, setting both times too short results in (possibly unwanted) artifacts.

In this case, the levels must all be nonzero and the have the same sign. \sine \sin sinusoidal S shaped segment. \welch \wel sinusoidal segment shaped like the sides of a Welch window. \squared \sqr squared segment \cubed \cub cubed segment

argDocs.freq: Frequency in Hertz. Positive frequencies only. WARNING: VarSaw will go out of range if the frequency exceeds the sampling rate (which for control rate is s.sampleRate / s.options.blockSize ).
argDocs.width: Duty cycle, denoting where in the cycle the waveform peaks. E.g. for widths of 0, 0.5, or 1.0 , the waveform will peak at the beginning, middle, or end of the cycle, respectively. [0..1] (clipped internally to [0.001..0.999])
argDocs.mul: The output will be multiplied by this value.
argDocs.add: This value will be added to the output.

ugens.name: Vibrato
ugens.summary: The Vibrato oscillator models a slow frequency modulation.

argDocs.freq: Fundamental frequency in Hertz. If the Vibrato UGen is running at audio rate, this must not be a constant, but an actual audio rate UGen (see example below)
argDocs.rate: Vibrato rate, speed of wobble in Hertz. Note that if this is set to a low value (and definitely with 0.0), you may never get vibrato back, since the rate input is only checked at the end of a cycle.
argDocs.depth: Size of vibrato frequency deviation around the fundamental, as a proportion of the fundamental. 0.02 = 2% of the fundamental.
argDocs.delay: Delay before vibrato is established in seconds (a singer tends to attack a note and then stabilise with vibrato, for instance).
argDocs.onset: Transition time in seconds from no vibrato to full vibrato after the initial delay time.
argDocs.rateVariation: Noise on the rate, expressed as a proportion of the rate; can change once per cycle of vibrato.
argDocs.depthVariation: Noise on the depth of modulation, expressed as a proportion of the depth; can change once per cycle of vibrato. The noise affects independently the up and the down part of vibrato shape within a cycle.
argDocs.iphase: Initial phase of vibrato modulation, allowing starting above or below the fundamental rather than on it.
argDocs.trig: Start again if transition from trig <= 0 to trig > 0.

argDocs.bufnum: the buffer number of a mono soundfile.
argDocs.pointer: the position in the buffer. The value should be between 0 and 1, with 0 being the beginning of the buffer, and 1 the end.
argDocs.freqScale: the amount of frequency shift. 1.0 is normal, 0.5 is one octave down, 2.0 is one octave up. Negative values play the soundfile backwards.
argDocs.windowSize: the size of each grain window.
argDocs.envbufnum: the buffer number containing a signal to use for the grain envelope. -1 uses a built-in Hanning envelope.
argDocs.windowRandRatio: the amount of randomness to the windowing function. Must be between 0 (no randomness) to 1.0 (probably too random actually)
argDocs.interp: the interpolation method used for pitchshifting grains. 1 = no interpolation. 2 = linear. 4 = cubic interpolation (more computationally intensive).
